All five acceptance criteria verified by direct execution, not by trusting the shipped tests:

Scope: only two files exist under the snapshot root — src/slug.js (one pure function, 33 lines) and test/slug.test.js. No package.json, lockfile, or config, so the dependency-risk surface is empty.

Checks performed against the security remit:

1. Injection / output safety — src/slug.js:14 replaces every character outside [a-z0-9] with a separator, so the output alphabet is provably [a-z0-9-]. Fuzzed 20,000 random strings over U+0001-U+2FFF: zero characters outside that set, no '/', '%', or '..' sequences, no leading/trailing hyphen, no result exceeding 60 chars. slugify('..%2f..%2fetc/passwd') === '2f-2fetc-passwd'. Path traversal and encoding smuggling are structurally impossible through this function.

2. ReDoS — the sole regex /[^a-z0-9]+/g (src/slug.js:14) is a single character class with one quantifier; no nesting or alternation, so no catastrophic backtracking. Measured 200 KB inputs of '!', alternating 'a!', and leading whitespace: all complete in <= 10.5 ms (linear).

3. Unbounded work — the accumulation loop at src/slug.js:24-29 breaks on the first overflowing word rather than continuing, so a 100,000-word title does bounded work.

4. Sensitive data in errors/logs — the TypeError at src/slug.js:9 uses a fixed message and does not interpolate the caller's argument, so a non-string carrying sensitive content cannot leak into the error or stack. There is no logging anywhere in the module.

5. Authn/authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization — no I/O, network, filesystem, eval/Function, JSON.parse, or credential-shaped literals. Nothing in these categories has a surface here.

Considered and deliberately not reported: AC2 mandates an empty-string output for punctuation-only titles, which a caller composing `/articles/${slug}` could turn into an ambiguous route. That is a property of a hypothetical caller rather than a defect in this code, and uniqueness is an explicit non-goal in the plan.

findings.title: `.filter(Boolean)` on the word list is unreachable-effect code: the preceding regex collapse plus trim guarantees `split(' ')` never yields a falsy element that changes the result.
findings.summary: In `slugify`, the pipeline is `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, ' ').trim().split(' ').filter(Boolean)`. Because the character class is quantified with `+`, every run of non-alphanumeric characters collapses to exactly one space, and `.trim()` removes the leading/trailing ones, so `split(' ')` can only produce non-empty words. The single exception is an input that reduces to `''`, where `split(' ')` returns `['']` — and that produces `''` either way, since `''.slice(0, MAX_LENGTH)` is `''` and the `for` loop over `words.slice(1)` has nothing to iterate.
findings.failure_scenario: No behavioral failure — that is the point. For `slugify('!!! ???')` the filter turns `['']` into `[]` and the `words.length === 0` guard returns `''`; with the filter deleted, `words` is `['']`, the guard is skipped, and line 23 returns `''` anyway. I verified equivalence exhaustively by running both variants over every string of length 0-5 built from `a`, `1`, `' '`, `'  '`, `-`, `!`, tab, and `é` (37,449 inputs): zero divergences. So the filter is dead, and with it gone the `words.length === 0` early return on lines 19-21 is also redundant, making the function three lines shorter with identical output for every input.

notes: All five acceptance criteria have at least one test and all 8 tests pass under `node --test`. No flakiness surface: slugify is pure with no clock, network, randomness, filesystem, or shared mutable state, and the tests are order-independent. The boundary tests at slug.test.js:43 and :51 are strong - they pin the `>` vs `>=` comparison from both sides. The AC5 test at :32 correctly asserts the guard's own message rather than just the TypeError class, which is the distinction that would otherwise let guard deletion pass. Reviewed only src/slug.js and test/slug.test.js (the only two files in the snapshot); no git commands were run and the reviewed tree was left byte-identical - mutation testing was performed on copies under the session scratchpad. Both findings are minor: the shipped implementation is correct, and each gap closes with one added assertion or case.

findings.title: The only test for AC4 asserts the slug's length but not its content, using an input where every possible 60-character result is identical, so it cannot detect truncation from the wrong end of the word.
findings.summary: Test 'a single word longer than MAX_LENGTH is cut to it' calls slugify('z'.repeat(100)) and asserts only assert.strictEqual(slug.length, MAX_LENGTH). Because every character of the input is 'z', any 60-character output passes regardless of which 60 characters the implementation kept. AC4 requires the word 'cut to exactly 60', i.e. the leading 60 characters.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by mutation on a scratch copy: changing src/slug.js:23 from `words[0].slice(0, MAX_LENGTH)` to `words[0].slice(-MAX_LENGTH)` leaves all 8 tests passing (# pass 8 # fail 0). With that regression in place, slugify('Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious'.repeat(3)) returns 'ifragilisticexpialidocioussupercalifragilisticexpialidocious' (the trailing 60 chars) instead of the correct 'supercalifragilisticexpialidocioussupercalifragilisticexpial'. Article URLs would be built from the tail of the title with the beginning silently discarded, and the suite would stay green.

findings.title: No test exercises a too-long word followed by a shorter word that would still fit, so the `break` that implements AC3's 'stops at the last whole word that fits' is unguarded; replacing it with `continue` passes the entire suite.
findings.summary: The over-length cases are slug.test.js:21 (all trailing words the same length, so skip-vs-stop is indistinguishable) and slug.test.js:52 ('a'x50 + ' ' + 'b'x10, where the rejected word is the last one). Neither has a word after the first rejected one, so the loop-termination semantics at src/slug.js:26 are never observed.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by mutation on a scratch copy: changing `break` to `continue` at src/slug.js:26 leaves all 8 tests passing (# pass 8 # fail 0). With that regression, slugify('a'.repeat(50) + ' ' + 'b'.repeat(10) + ' c') returns 'aaaa...a-c' (52 chars) instead of the AC3-correct 'aaaa...a' (50 chars) - a slug that drops a word out of the middle of the title while still satisfying the length bound and the no-trailing-hyphen rule that the current assertions check.
